text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, in Malaysia for an official visit, met with Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and said relations between the two countries have strengthened tremendously.
-- The Sabah state government said Diriwan Corp Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Olympia Industries Bhd, will not be allowed to resume its gaming operations in the state.

-- Bus operator Intrakota Consolidated Sdn Bhd, a unit of Diversified Resources, has pledged to improve its services in the Klang Valley by next week, said Deputy Entrepreneur Development Minister Idris Jusoh. This follows public complaints that there were not enough buses on the road since Intrakota took over the services of 400 mini-buses.
-- National car maker Proton plans to introduce a totally Malaysian made car in the near future, said a company vice-chairman Tengku Mahaleel Tengku Ariff.
-- The government has approved national carrier Malaysian Airline System Bhd to increase fares by three percent on all its international routes, said Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik.
